items.title: Low Dose Ketamine Preconditions Astrocyte Mitochondria to Achieve Antidepressant Efficacy via Adenosine, Humanin, and Melatonin Upregulation and Efflux.

summaries.en: New research reveals that ketamine's antidepressant power might work differently than we thought — not by blocking brain signals, but by tuning up the energy factories inside support cells called astrocytes. When these cellular powerhouses function better, they seem to restore mood and resilience. Scientists reviewed extensive evidence to propose that ketamine directly optimizes mitochondrial function, with ripple effects across the brain. This finding matters because it could lead to faster, more targeted depression treatments with fewer side effects. As psychedelics research accelerates, understanding these precise cellular mechanisms — rather than relying on older theories — is opening doors to smarter therapeutics that address what actually goes wrong in depression.
summaries.da: Ny forskning viser, at ketamins antidepressive kraft muligvis virker anderledes end antaget — ikke ved at blokere hjernens signaler, men ved at justere energifabrikkerne inden i støtteceller kaldet astrocytter. Når disse cellulære kraftværker fungerer bedre, synes de at genoprette humør og resiliens. Forskere gennemgik omfattende evidens for at foreslå, at ketamin direkte optimerer mitokondriefunktion, med ringvirkninger på tværs af hjernen. Dette fund betyder noget, fordi det kunne føre til hurtigere, mere målrettede depressionsforsøg med færre bivirkninger. Mens psykedelika-forskning accelererer, er forståelsen af disse præcise cellulære mekanismer — snarere end at stole på ældre teorier — ved at åbne døre til smartere terapier, der behandler det, der faktisk går galt ved depression.

items.title: Healing together: Results from a pilot trial of 3,4‐Methylenedioxymethamphetamine‐enhanced cognitive‐behavioral conjoint therapy for posttraumatic stress disorder

summaries.en: What if trauma therapy could actually heal relationships, not just individual wounds? A pilot study of military couples found that when MDMA was combined with couples therapy, veterans saw major drops in PTSD symptoms—and both partners reported dramatic improvements in how they connected with each other. That's the striking part: traditional trauma therapy often helps the person but leaves relationships struggling. This small study of eight veteran couples received eight sessions of MDMA-assisted therapy designed specifically to strengthen their bond while treating trauma. The results hint at something bigger happening in psychedelics research right now—a shift toward using these tools not just to fix what's broken inside us, but to rebuild what's broken between us.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis traumebehandling kunne hele forhold i stedet for bare individuelle sår? Et pilotprojekt med militærpar viste, at når MDMA blev kombineret med parterapi, oplevede veteraner drastiske fald i PTSD-symptomer—og begge partnere rapporterede dramatiske forbedringer i deres gensidige forbindelse. Det er det slående: traditionel traumabehandling hjælper ofte den enkelte, men efterlader forhold i krise. Denne lille undersøgelse af otte veteranpar gennemgik otte sessionener MDMA-assisteret terapi designet specifikt til at styrke deres bånd mens de behandlede traumer. Resultaterne antyder noget større i psykedelika-forskningen lige nu—et skift mod at bruge disse værktøjer ikke bare til at reparere hvad der er ødelagt inden i os, men til at genopbygge hvad der er ødelagt mellem os.

items.title: Hallucinogen Persisting Perception Disorder in a Young Adult Case Report.

summaries.en: What happens when hallucinations don't fade? A 24-year-old experienced persistent visual disturbances—flickering, snow-like patterns—months after using LSD, a rare condition called HPPD that can stick around long after the trip ends. Combined with bipolar disorder and anxiety, his case shows how tricky these lingering perceptual changes can be to diagnose and treat, especially when they blur into psychiatric symptoms. Researchers studied his clinical journey through medication trials and therapy, finding that while his visual symptoms never completely disappeared, he achieved stability and learned to live with them. As psychedelics like LSD move into clinical research for treating anxiety and depression, understanding these rare but real persistent side effects becomes crucial—not to scare people away, but to help clinicians recognize them, support patients properly, and ensure psychedelic science develops with eyes wide open to both benefits and risks.
summaries.da: Hvad sker der når hallucinations ikke forsvinder? En 24-årig oplevede vedvarende visuelle forstyrrelser—flimren, sneagtige mønstre—måneder efter at have brugt LSD, en sjælden tilstand kaldet HPPD, som kan blive ved længe efter tripet er slut. Kombineret med bipolær lidelse og angst viser hans tilfælde hvor knivskarp diagnosticeringen og behandlingen af disse vedvarende perceptuelle ændringer kan være, især når de blandes med psykiatriske symptomer. Forskere studerede hans kliniske forløb gennem medicinforsøg og terapi og fandt, at selvom hans visuelle symptomer aldrig helt forsvandt, opnåede han stabilitet og lærte at leve med dem. Efterhånden som psykedelika som LSD bevæger sig ind i klinisk forskning for angst og depression, bliver forståelsen af disse sjældne men reelle vedvarende bivirkninger afgørende—ikke for at skræmme folk væk, men for at hjælpe klinikere med at genkende dem, støtte patienterne ordentligt og sikre, at psykedelisk videnskab udvikler sig med åbne øjne for både fordele og risici.

items.title: Network Pharmacology Reveals the Potential Mechanism of Ketamine in Improving Cognitive Impairment in Patients With Depression.

summaries.en: Ketamine isn't just lifting depression—it might also be sharpening the foggy thinking that often comes with it. A new study mapped out how ketamine works at the molecular level, discovering it influences at least 20 key proteins in the brain linked to both mood and cognition. The researchers used advanced bioinformatics to trace ketamine's pathways, finding it particularly affects dopamine signaling and inflammation in the brain. This matters because cognitive problems—trouble concentrating, memory gaps, mental fatigue—are a huge part of depression that often gets overlooked. As psychedelics research expands beyond symptom relief toward actual brain healing, understanding ketamine's multi-target approach gives us a clearer picture of how these molecules might restore not just mood, but mental clarity too.
summaries.da: Ketamin løfter ikke bare depressionen—det kan også være med til at få den tågede tænkning til at klare sig igen. Et nyt studie kortlagde, hvordan ketamin virker på molekylært niveau, og opdagede at det påvirker mindst 20 vigtige hjerneceller forbundet med både humør og kognitiv funktion. Forskerne brugte avanceret bioinformatik til at spore ketamins signalveje og fandt ud af, at det især påvirker dopaminsignalering og betændelse i hjernen. Det betyder noget, fordi kognitive problemer—svært ved at koncentrere sig, hukommelseshuller, mental træthed—er en stor del af depression, som ofte bliver overset. Mens psykedelika-forskningen udvider sig fra symptomlindrende behandling mod faktisk hjerneheling, giver forståelsen af ketamins flertarget-tilgang os et klarere billede af, hvordan disse molekyler kan genoprette ikke bare humøret, men også den mentale klarhed.

items.title: Pα+ Library: Psychedelic REMS

summaries.en:
As psychedelic therapies inch closer to FDA approval, a crucial question looms: how will they actually reach patients? New attention is turning to REMS—Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies—the safety frameworks that will likely shape how these treatments are delivered in the real world. Think of it as the guardrails that could make psychedelic therapy accessible while keeping people safe.

Researchers are mapping out what REMS might look like for psychedelics, examining how other regulated medicines have used these frameworks. This matters because it's not just about whether these therapies work in studies—it's about building the infrastructure to deliver them responsibly when they're available to you. As psychedelic research accelerates from lab to clinic, understanding REMS is becoming essential to the bigger picture of how breakthrough treatments actually become part of mainstream medicine.
summaries.da:
Efterhånden som psykedelika-terapier nærmer sig FDA-godkendelse, dukker et afgørende spørgsmål op: hvordan kommer de egentlig til patienterne? Opmærksomheden rettes nu mod REMS—Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies—de sikkerhedsmekanismer, der sandsynligvis kommer til at forme hvordan disse behandlinger leveres i praksis. Tænk på det som skinnerne, der kan gøre psykedelika-terapi tilgængelig og samtidig holde folk sikre.

Forsker kortlægger hvordan REMS kunne se ud for psykedelika ved at undersøge hvordan andre regulerede lægemidler har brugt disse systemer. Det betyder noget, fordi det ikke blot handler om at terapierne virker i studier—det handler om at bygge infrastrukturen til at levere dem ansvarligt når de bliver tilgængelige for dig. Som psykedelika-forskningen accelererer fra laboratorium til klinik, bliver forståelsen af REMS central for det større billede af hvordan gennembrudsterapier faktisk bliver del af almindelig medicin.

items.title: Healing together: Results from a pilot trial of 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine-enhanced cognitive-behavioral conjoint therapy for posttraumatic stress disorder.

summaries.en: What if healing from trauma didn't just help you—it helped your relationship too? A new pilot study gave eight military veterans with PTSD and their partners MDMA-assisted therapy combined with couples counseling. The results were striking: veterans saw major drops in PTSD symptoms, but here's the real breakthrough—both partners reported huge improvements in how they connected with each other, with gains that stuck around months later. Researchers used a structured eight-session protocol with two MDMA sessions woven into couples therapy, tracking both trauma recovery and relationship health. This fits into a growing shift in psychedelic research: moving beyond treating individual symptoms toward healing the whole person, including their most important relationships. For veterans especially, where deployment and trauma can shatter bonds with loved ones, this suggests psychedelics might help rebuild what war breaks apart.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis det at hele sig fra traumer ikke bare hjalp dig—men også dit forhold? Et nyt pilotprojekt gav otte militærveteraner med PTSD og deres partnere MDMA-assisteret terapi kombineret med parterapi. Resultaterne var slående: veteranerne så store fald i PTSD-symptomer, men her er det virkelige gennembrud—begge partnere rapporterede enorme forbedringer i, hvordan de forbandt med hinanden, med resultater der holdt måneder senere. Forskerne brugte et struktureret otte-sessionsprogram med to MDMA-sessioner vævet ind i parterapi, hvor de sporede både traume-helbredelse og forhold-sundhed. Dette passer ind i en voksende forskning med psykedelika: væk fra at behandle individuelle symptomer hen imod at hele hele mennesket, inklusive deres vigtigste forhold. For veteraner især, hvor udsendelser og traumer kan ødelægge bånd til elskede, tyder dette på at psykedelika kan hjælpe med at genopbygge hvad krig ødelægger.

items.title: Psilocybin prevents chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy through mitochondrial trafficking preservation.

summaries.en: Millions of cancer patients suffer from chemotherapy's brutal side effect: nerve damage that can steal sensation from their fingers and toes, sometimes permanently. New research just showed that a couple of doses of psilocybin before chemo could prevent this from happening—without weakening the cancer treatment itself. Scientists gave psilocybin to mice before chemotherapy and found it protected the tiny nerve endings in their skin by keeping the energy powerhouses inside nerve cells working properly, while also steadying brain activity. This is one of those rare moments where psychedelics might offer something medicine has been desperately searching for: a real solution to a problem that affects millions. As psychedelic research moves from 'fascinating molecules' into 'concrete treatments for hard-to-solve problems,' this finding is exactly the kind of bridge between traditional medicine and these remarkable compounds that could change how we think about cancer care.
summaries.da: Millioner af kræftpatienter lider under kemoterapiens grusom bivirkning: nerveskader der kan tage følelsen fra fingre og tæer, nogle gange permanent. Ny forskning viser netop, at et par doser psykedelika før kemoterapien kunne forhindre dette – uden at svække selve kræftbehandlingen. Forskere gav psykedelika til mus før kemoterapien og fandt ud af, at det beskyttede de små nerveender i deres hud ved at holde energikraftværkerne inde i nerveceller i gang, mens det samtidig stabiliserede hjernens aktivitet. Dette er et af de sjældne øjeblikke, hvor psykedelika kunne tilbyde noget som medicinen desperat har søgt efter: en rigtig løsning på et problem som påvirker millioner. Når psykedelisk forskning bevæger sig fra 'fascinerende molekyler' til 'konkrete behandlinger for svært løselige problemer', er denne opdagelse præcis den slags bro mellem traditionel medicin og disse bemærkelsesværdige stoffer som kunne ændre på hvordan vi tænker kræftbehandling.

items.title: Safety, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of intravenously administered deuterated

summaries.en:
Scientists just tested a new modified version of DMT called CYB004 in humans—and it's a game-changer for how long the experience lasts. While regular DMT's effects fade in minutes, this deuterated version kept people in the psychedelic state for 40-60 minutes, giving researchers a much bigger window to study what's actually happening in the brain. The catch? Higher doses triggered intense experiences that made some participants drop out, but lower doses proved safe and well-tolerated, opening doors for future research.

This was a rigorous, controlled study where healthy volunteers received carefully measured IV doses while scientists tracked their brain activity, vital signs, and subjective experiences. It's a perfect example of how psychedelic research is evolving—moving beyond asking "is this safe?" to asking "how can we optimize these compounds to learn more?" By extending the duration without changing the fundamental effects, CYB004 gives neuroscientists a better tool to map exactly how psychedelics reshape consciousness and potentially treat conditions like depression and PTSD.
summaries.da:
Forskere har netop testet en ny modificeret version af DMT kaldet CYB004 på mennesker—og det er game-changing for, hvor længe oplevelsen varer. Mens almindelig DMT's effekter forsvinder på minutter, holdt denne deutererede version mennesker i psykedelisk tilstand i 40-60 minutter, hvilket giver forskerne et langt større tidsvindue til at studere, hvad der faktisk sker i hjernen. Fangsten? Højere doser udløste intense oplevelser, der fik nogle forsøgspersoner til at melde sig ud, men lavere doser viste sig sikre og veltolererede, hvilket åbner døre for fremtidig forskning.

Dette var et stringent, kontrolleret studie, hvor raske frivillige fik nøje målte IV-doser, mens forskere fulgte deres hjernaktivitet, vitale tegn og subjektive oplevelser. Det er et perfekt eksempel på, hvordan psykedelika-forskning udvikler sig—ud over at spørge "er dette sikkert?" til at spørge "hvordan kan vi optimere disse stoffer for at lære mere?" Ved at forlænge varigheden uden at ændre de grundlæggende effekter, giver CYB004 neuroforskere et bedre værktøj til at kortlægge præcist, hvordan psykedelika omformer bevidstheden og potentielt behandler tilstande som depression og PTSD.

items.title: Implementing psychedelic-assisted therapy in Ireland: perspectives from a national stakeholder survey.

summaries.en: Ireland is quietly gearing up for psychedelic-assisted therapy — and people working in healthcare, mental health, and policy actually want it to happen. A new survey asked stakeholders across the country what they think about bringing these treatments into clinical practice, and the picture that emerged is surprisingly hopeful: there's real appetite for change, but also clear-eyed questions about how to do it right. The researchers talked to people on the front lines — therapists, doctors, policymakers — to understand what Ireland needs to make this work practically and safely. This kind of groundwork matters enormously. As psychedelics move from research labs toward real clinics, countries need to figure out training, regulation, and integration. Ireland's survey is exactly the kind of thinking that turns scientific promise into actual healthcare change.
summaries.da: Irland forbereder sig stilfærdigt på psykedelika-assisteret terapi — og mennesker i sundhedsvæsen, psykisk helbred og politik ønsker faktisk at det skal ske. En ny survey spurgte interessenter på tværs af landet, hvad de mener om at bringe disse behandlinger ind i klinisk praksis, og billedet der tegner sig er overraskende håbefuldt: der er ægte appetit på forandring, men også klare spørgsmål om at gøre det rigtigt. Forskerne talte med mennesker på frontlinjen — terapeuter, læger, politikere — for at forstå hvad Irland har brug for for at få det til at virke praktisk og sikkert. Den slags forberedende arbejde betyder enormt meget. Når psykedelika bevæger sig fra forsøgslaboratorier mod rigtige klinikker, skal landene finde ud af træning, regulering og integration. Irlands survey er præcis den slags tænkning der omdanner videnskabelig løfte til faktisk sundhedsændring.

items.title: The subtle science: a systematic review of psilocybin magic mushroom and truffle microdosing.

summaries.en: People microdosing psilocybin report feeling better mentally, more creative, and sharper cognitively — but here's the honest part: most of this evidence comes from people's own accounts rather than rigorous lab testing, so we need to be careful about what we actually know versus what people hope is true. Researchers reviewed 11 studies involving over 3,200 adults from across the globe to map out what's being claimed about microdosing magic mushrooms and truffles. The findings reveal a curious gap: while roughly 86% of people microdose for personal wellness rather than medical reasons, the scientific picture remains blurry. This review highlights exactly where psychedelic research stands right now — we're at the stage of listening closely to what people experience, but we urgently need more controlled studies to separate genuine effects from placebo and expectation. It's the kind of groundwork that makes future breakthroughs possible.
summaries.da: Folk der microdoser psilocybin rapporterer om bedre mental sundhed, mere kreativitet og skarpere hjerner — men her er det ærlige: det meste af denne evidens kommer fra menneskers egne erfaringer snarere end stiv laboratorieforskning, så vi skal være forsigtige med hvad vi egentlig ved versus hvad folk håber på. Forskere gennemgik 11 studier med over 3.200 voksne fra hele verden for at kortlægge hvad der bliver hævdet om microdosering af magiske svampe og trøfler. Fundet afslører et interessant hul: mens cirka 86% microdoser for personlig velbefindende snarere end medicinske årsager, er det videnskabelige billede uklart. Denne oversigt viser præcis hvor psykedelika-forskningen står nu — vi er på stadiet hvor vi lytter tæt til hvad mennesker oplever, men vi har desperat brug for flere kontrollerede studier for at skelne ægte effekter fra placebo og forventning. Det er den slags grundarbejde, der gør fremtidige gennembrud mulige.

items.title: Serial Ketamine Infusions for Treatment-Resistant Bipolar Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

summaries.en: When standard antidepressants fail people with bipolar depression, hope runs thin. But a new Canadian trial shows ketamine infusions might offer real relief: people who received four doses of ketamine over two weeks saw significant drops in depression symptoms, outperforming the control group. The catch? We still need to watch carefully for mood destabilization, since bipolar brains respond differently than others. Researchers gave ketamine intravenously in a rigorous, double-blind study with people who'd already tried at least two other treatments without success. This matters because bipolar depression is notoriously hard to treat—existing drugs often fall flat. As psychedelics move beyond hype into serious clinical testing, this research shows us ketamine's potential in populations previously considered too risky. The question now isn't whether it works, but how to use it safely and wisely.
summaries.da: Når almindelige antidepressiva ikke virker for mennesker med bipolar depression, bliver håbet lille. Men et nyt canadisk forsøg viser, at psykedelika som ketamin kan give ægte lindring: mennesker som fik fire doser ketamin over to uger oplevede betydelige fald i depressionssymptomer og klarede sig bedre end kontrolgruppen. Hagen? Vi skal være opmærksomme på humørsvingninger, fordi bipolare hjerner reagerer anderledes end andre. Forskerne gav ketamin intravenøst i et grundigt, dobbeltblindt studie med mennesker, som allerede havde prøvet mindst to andre behandlinger uden succes. Det betyder noget, fordi bipolar depression er notorisk svær at behandle—eksisterende lægemidler fungerer ofte ikke. Mens psykedelika bevæger sig fra hype mod seriøs klinisk forskning, viser denne undersøgelse ketamins potentiale hos befolkningsgrupper, der tidligere blev betragtet som for risikofyldt. Spørgsmålet nu er ikke længere, om det virker, men hvordan man bruger det sikkert og klogt.

items.title: Real-world clinical practice, effectiveness and safety of esketamine nasal spray in major depressive disorder patients: a French prospective cohort (ELLIPSE study).

summaries.en: After years of hitting dead ends with antidepressants, many people with severe depression still had nowhere to turn. A new French study followed 200 patients with treatment-resistant depression who tried esketamine nasal spray—and found that over half experienced significant symptom relief within two months, with one-third reaching remission. The improvements stuck around for a full year. Researchers tracked real patients in actual clinics (not just controlled lab settings) between 2021 and 2023, measuring their depression scores month by month. While side effects like brief dissociative states happened in about two-thirds of patients, they were generally manageable. This matters because it's the first large real-world evidence that esketamine actually works outside of clinical trials—filling a crucial gap in our understanding of how this promising treatment performs when doctors use it in everyday practice. As psychedelics move from counterculture to clinical reality, studies like this are essential for understanding what works for whom.
summaries.da: Efter år med at slå hovedet mod muren med almindelige antidepressiva havde mange mennesker med alvorlig depression intet håb tilbage. Et nyt fransk studie fulgte 200 patienter med behandlingsresistent depression, der prøvede esketamin-næsespray—og fandt ud af, at over halvdelen oplevede betydelig symptombedring inden for to måneder, og en tredjedel nåede fuldstændig remission. Forbedringerne holdt sig hele året. Forskerne fulgte rigtige patienter i almindelige klinikker (ikke kun kontrollerede laboratorieforhold) mellem 2021 og 2023 og målte deres depressionsscore måned efter måned. Selvom bivirkninger som kortvarig dissociation forekom hos omkring to tredjedel af patienterne, var de generelt håndterbare. Det betyder noget, fordi det er det første større bevis fra virkeligheden for, at psykedelika som esketamin faktisk virker uden for kliniske forsøg—og udfylder et afgørende hul i vores forståelse. Mens psykedelika bevæger sig fra modkultur til klinisk virkelighed, er sådanne studier vigtige for at forstå hvad der virker for hvem.

items.title: Measuring the contents of hallucinations from psychedelics and stroboscopic light: the Six-Dimensional Visual Hallucination Questionnaire

summaries.en: What exactly do you see when you're on psychedelics? Researchers just created a precise tool to measure it. The new Six-Dimensional Visual Hallucination Questionnaire breaks down what people experience into six key elements—from geometric patterns and detail level to how vivid and focused the visions are. Testing it on nearly 1,000 people, they found something fascinating: psychedelics produce hallucinations packed with meaning and intricate detail, while simple strobe lights trigger mostly basic geometric shapes. This matters because understanding the texture of hallucinations—what's actually happening in your visual experience—helps scientists decode how the brain constructs reality itself.
summaries.da: Hvad ser du præcist, når du tager psykedelika? Forskere har netop udviklet et præcist værktøj til at måle det. Det nye Six-Dimensional Visual Hallucination Questionnaire opdeler det, mennesker oplever, i seks nøgleelementer—fra geometriske mønstre og detaljegrad til hvor levende og fokuseret visioner er. Da de testede det på næsten 1.000 mennesker, opdagede de noget fascinerende: psykedelika producerer hallucinationer fulde af betydning og indviklede detaljer, mens simple strobelys primært udløser basale geometriske former. Det betyder noget, fordi når videnskabsmænd forstår teksturen af hallucinationer—hvad der rent faktisk foregår i din visuelle oplevelse—hjælper det dem med at tyde, hvordan hjernen konstruerer virkeligheden selv.

items.title: Through the Looking-Glass: A Scoping Review of Psychological Mechanisms of Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy for Substance Use Disorders

summaries.en: What if the key to breaking free from addiction lies not in willpower alone, but in a profound shift in how you see yourself and the world? A major review of 37 studies shows that psychedelics like psilocybin, ketamine, and MDMA appear to rewire people's relationship with substance use by triggering deep emotional breakthroughs, mystical experiences, and a fundamental reimagining of identity and values. Researchers analyzed over 1,000 people across these studies and found six core ways psychedelics seem to work their magic: emotional processing, meaning-making, identity transformation, mystical experiences, stronger relationships, and renewed motivation. The science is still early, but the pattern is clear: psychedelics aren't just another medical tool—they're opening a completely different door to how we treat addiction, one that works through psychological and spiritual dimensions we're only beginning to understand.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis nøglen til at bryde fri fra afhængighed ikke blot ligger i vilje, men i en dyb omkalfatring af, hvordan du ser dig selv og verden? En omfattende analyse af 37 studier viser, at psykedelika som psilocybin, ketamin og MDMA synes at omvurdere menneskers forhold til stofmisbrug ved at udløse dybe følelsesmæssige gennembrud, mystiske oplevelser og en grundlæggende omtolkning af identitet og værdier. Forskere analyserede over 1.000 mennesker på tværs af studierne og fandt seks centrale mekanismer: følelsesbehandling, meningsskabelse, identitetstransformation, mystiske erfaringer, styrket relationer og fornyet motivation. Videnskaben er stadig i sin vorden, men mønsteret er klart: psykedelika er ikke bare endnu et medicinsk værktøj—de åbner en helt anden dør til, hvordan vi behandler afhængighed, en der arbejder gennem psykologiske og åndelige dimensioner, som vi først er ved at forstå.

items.title: Surrender, disidentification, and reappraisal: a qualitative comparison of psilocybin responders and non-responders in treatment-resistant OCD

summaries.en: What's the difference between someone with OCD who finds relief through psilocybin and someone who doesn't? A new study reveals something striking: responders tend to surrender to their experience rather than fight it, and they develop self-compassion instead of being trapped in their obsessions. Researchers compared six participants from a psilocybin trial—three who improved significantly and three who didn't—through detailed interviews a month after their session. They found that those who benefited experienced a genuine shift: they could separate themselves from their OCD thoughts, feel emotions fully in their body, and suddenly see their obsessions as less meaningful. This research reveals the active ingredients of psychedelic healing aren't just chemical—the psychological moves people make during and after the experience matter enormously. As scientists explore psychedelics for stubborn mental health conditions, understanding who benefits and why is crucial for making these treatments work better for more people.
summaries.da: Hvad adskiller mennesker med OCD, der finder lindring gennem psykedelika, fra dem der ikke gør? Et nyt studie afslører noget slående: dem der bliver bedre har en tendens til at overgive sig til deres oplevelse i stedet for at kæmpe imod, og de udvikler selvmedlidenhed i stedet for at være fanget i deres tvangstanker. Forskere sammenlignede seks deltagere fra et psykedelika-forsøg—tre som blev markant bedre og tre som ikke blev det—gennem detaljerede samtaler en måned efter deres session. De fandt, at dem som fik gavn oplevede et ægte skifte: de kunne adskille sig selv fra deres OCD-tanker, føle følelser fuldt ud i kroppen, og pludselig se deres tvangstanker som mindre betydningsfulde. Denne forskning viser, at de aktive ingredienser i psykedelisk helbredelse ikke blot er kemiske—de psykologiske bevægelser mennesker gør under og efter oplevelsen betyder enormt. Mens forskere udforsker psykedelika til stædig psykisk sygdom, er det afgørende for succes at forstå hvem der bliver bedre og hvorfor.

items.title: Age and Cannabis Co-Use Are Associated with Differences in Experience and Perceived Benefits of Psilocybin: A Retrospective Study.

summaries.en: Here's something surprising: younger people taking psilocybin report way more uncomfortable experiences than older adults—but it doesn't actually stop them from getting the deeper insights everyone seeks. A new study of 365 psilocybin users found that age shapes the *ride* you have, not necessarily where you end up. Even more intriguing? People who combined psilocybin with cannabis reported significantly better improvements in anxiety, depression, and quality of life, hinting at unexpected synergies between the two substances. Researchers surveyed people across three age groups (18-77) about their experiences, and the pattern was clear: youth brought intensity, age brought smoothness, and cannabis appeared to amplify therapeutic benefits. As psychedelics become more accessible, understanding these individual differences matters—not to scare anyone off, but to help people and researchers know what to expect and how to work with it.
summaries.da: Her er noget overraskende: unge mennesker, der tager psilocybin, rapporterer betydeligt flere ubehagelige oplevelser end ældre voksne—men det stopper dem ikke i at få de dybere indsigter, alle søger. Et nyt studie af 365 psilocybin-brugere viser, at alder former *turen*, du oplever, ikke nødvendigvis hvor du ender hen. Endnu mere fascinerende? Mennesker, der kombinerede psilocybin med cannabis, rapporterede markant større forbedringer i angst, depression og livskvalitet—hvilket tyder på uventede synergi mellem de to stoffer. Forskere spurgte mennesker på tværs af tre aldersgrupper (18-77 år) om deres oplevelser, og mønsteret var klart: ungdom bragte intensitet, alder bragte glathes, og cannabis så ud til at forstærke terapeutiske fordele. Når psykedelika bliver mere tilgængelige, betyder det at forstå disse individuelle forskelle—ikke for at skræmme nogen væk, men for at hjælpe mennesker og forskere med at vide, hvad der venter, og hvordan man arbejder med det.

items.title: The mPFC-reuniens-hippocampus pathway links brain circuitry and neural plasticity in antidepressant response.

summaries.en:
Scientists just mapped out a crucial brain circuit that explains how antidepressants actually work—and the discovery could reshape how we think about treating depression. When researchers activated a specific brain region in depressed mice, it triggered a chain reaction: signals traveled to the hippocampus, rewired neural connections, and lifted depressive symptoms across the board. The key insight? A tiny relay station in the brain called the nucleus reuniens acts like a critical control center, linking brain circuit activity directly to the physical changes that help us feel better.

Using chemogenetic techniques in a mouse model of stress-induced depression, researchers identified this IL→RE→vHIPP pathway and then proved its necessity by blocking it—which erased both the antidepressant effect and, strikingly, the benefits of ketamine. This matters enormously because it suggests depression isn't just about one broken system but about how different brain regions communicate. As psychedelic research pushes deeper into how compounds like psilocybin reshape neural plasticity and connectivity, this kind of circuit mapping becomes essential knowledge—helping us understand not just what works, but why.
summaries.da:
Forskere har netop kortlagt et afgørende hjernekreds, der forklarer hvordan antidepressiva faktisk fungerer—og opdagelsen kunne ændre vores syn på behandling af depression. Da forskerne aktiverede et specifikt hjernområde hos deprimerede mus, udløste det en kaskade: signaler rejste til hippocampus, omvirkede neurale forbindelser og løftede depressive symptomer i hele linjen. Nøgleindsigten? Et lille relæstation i hjernen kaldet nucleus reuniens fungerer som et kritisk kontrolcenter, der direkte forbinder hjernekredsen aktivitet til de fysiske ændringer, der hjælper os til at have det bedre.

Ved hjælp af kemogenetiske teknikker i en musemodel med stressudløst depression identificerede forskerne denne IL→RE→vHIPP-bane og beviste derefter dens nødvendighed ved at blokere den—hvilket udsletted både antidepressiv effekt og bemærkelsesværdigt fordelene ved ketamin. Dette betyder enormt meget, fordi det antyder, at depression ikke blot handler om ét ødelagt system, men om hvordan forskellige hjerneregionforbindelser kommunikerer. Når psykedelika-forskning presser dybere ind i hvordan forbindelser som psilocybin omformer neural plasticitet og konnektivitet, bliver denne slags kredskorttægning vigtig viden—og hjælper os forstå ikke bare hvad der virker, men hvorfor.

items.title: Factors Associated with Intentions to Use Psilocybin for Mental Health in Relation to Psychotherapy, Psychiatric Medications, and Natural/Synthetic Options.

summaries.en: People are increasingly curious about psilocybin as a mental health treatment—but what actually makes someone consider trying it? New research reveals that folks are most drawn to psilocybin when they see it working *alongside* therapy, not as a solo fix. Interestingly, people don't necessarily view it as competing with psychiatric medications; many see it as a different path worth exploring. The study surveyed people's real attitudes toward psilocybin in mental health contexts, mapping out what builds trust and openness. This matters because as psychedelics move closer to clinical use, understanding what resonates with people—and why—helps shape how we talk about these tools. It's a reminder that the science is only half the story; the other half is how people actually feel about integrating something this novel into their care.
summaries.da: Flere og flere mennesker er nysgerrige på psykedelika som behandling for psykiske lidelser—men hvad får nogen til at overveje at prøve det? Ny forskning viser, at folk er mest tiltrukket af psykedelika når de ser det arbejde *sammen med* terapi, ikke som en selvstændig løsning. Interessant nok ser mennesker det ikke nødvendigvis som konkurrence med psykiatriske medicin; mange ser det som en anden vej værd at udforske. Studiet undersøgte menneskers rigtige holdninger til psykedelika i mental sundhed, og kortlagde hvad der bygger tillid og åbenhed. Det betyder noget, fordi når psykedelika kommer tættere på klinisk brug, hjælper det at forstå hvad der taler til mennesker—og hvorfor. Det er en påmindelse om, at videnskaben kun er halvdelen af historien; den anden halvdel er hvordan mennesker faktisk føler over for at integrere noget så nyt i deres behandling.

items.title: Can Psychedelics help with Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD): For now, the data says no.

summaries.en:
Here's a sobering reality check: despite the buzz around psychedelics for treating alcohol addiction, the science just isn't there yet. A new review found that while LSD, MDMA, and psilocybin show promise, the actual evidence for helping people with alcohol use disorder remains thin—many studies lack proper controls and follow-ups, making it hard to know what's really working. Meanwhile, FDA-approved medications like naltrexone already exist and do the job, yet almost nobody uses them (only 2% of patients get them). The real story here isn't that psychedelics are the answer—it's that we're sitting on effective treatments people don't even know about, wrapped in stigma and stuck in outdated systems.

So where do psychedelics fit in? Researchers aren't saying no forever. They're saying: let's do this properly. The takeaway for now is that psychedelics might eventually help people who've tried everything else and failed, but only if we run rigorous, well-designed studies. The bigger picture? We're at a moment where smarter drug policy, better access to existing medicines, and careful psychedelic research could all work together—but we need to be honest about what works today while we figure out what might work tomorrow.
summaries.da:
Her er en hård virkelighed: på trods af alt buzzen omkring psykedelika til behandling af alkoholafhængighed, så er videnskaben bare ikke på plads endnu. En ny oversigt fandt, at selvom LSD, MDMA og psilocybin viser potentiale, så er den faktiske evidens for at hjælpe mennesker med alkoholforgiftning stadig meget tynd—mange studier mangler ordentlige kontroller og opfølgninger, hvilket gør det svært at vide hvad der reelt virker. Samtidig eksisterer FDA-godkendte mediciner som naltrexon allerede og gør jobbet, men næsten ingen bruger dem (kun 2% af patienterne får dem). Den rigtige historie her er ikke, at psykedelika er svaret—det er, at vi sidder på effektive behandlinger som mennesker ikke engang ved eksisterer, omgærdet af stigma og fast i forældede systemer.

Så hvor passer psykedelika ind? Forskere siger ikke nej for evigt. De siger: lad os gøre det rigtigt. Det vigtigste for nu er, at psykedelika måske engang kan hjælpe mennesker som har prøvet alt andet uden resultat—men kun hvis vi gennemfører grundige, veldesignede studier. Det større billede? Vi er på et tidspunkt hvor smartere narkotikaudannelse, bedre adgang til eksisterende medicin og omhyggelig psykedelika-forskning kunne arbejde sammen—men vi skal være ærlige om hvad der virker i dag mens vi finder ud af hvad der måske virker i morgen.

items.title: Pα+ Psychedelic Bulletin #230: Pharma Ramps Up Ad Spend on Psychedelic Keywords; ARPA-H’s Ibogaine Funding; Psychedelics in Medicaid?

summaries.en:
Big pharma is betting big on psychedelics. Major pharmaceutical companies are flooding Google with ads about psychedelic treatments, with Johnson & Johnson leading the charge to promote Spravato, their ketamine-based depression drug. Meanwhile, the same search results now feature at-home ketamine clinics and wellness providers—a sign that psychedelic medicine is going mainstream, fast. This shift reveals something important: the industry sees real market potential here, and competition is heating up to reach people searching for alternatives to traditional antidepressants.

What's driving this? Government agencies like ARPA-H are backing research into psychedelics like ibogaine, and there's growing momentum to get these treatments covered by Medicaid. As the evidence builds and regulations loosen, we're watching the transformation of psychedelics from fringe therapy to serious medicine—complete with the corporate advertising machines that usually follow. The question now isn't whether psychedelics work; it's how quickly they'll become accessible to the people who need them most.
summaries.da:
Storfarmacias satser stort på psykedelika. Større medicinalfirmaer oversvømmer Google med annoncer om psykedelika-behandlinger, og Johnson & Johnson fører an med deres ketamin-baserede Spravato mod depression. Samtidigt dukker hjemmebaserede ketaminklinikker og wellness-udbydere op i de samme søgeresultater—et tegn på, at psykedelika-medicin bliver mainstream. Det afslører noget væsentligt: industrien ser virkelig markedspotentiale her, og konkurrencen bliver hårdere om at nå mennesker, der søger alternativer til traditionelle antidepressiva.

Hvad driver dette? Statslige agenturer som ARPA-H finansierer forskning i psykedelika som ibogain, og der er voksende momentum for at få disse behandlinger dækket af Medicaid. Efterhånden som evidensen vokser og regulering lempet op, ser vi psykedelika transformeres fra randzone-terapi til seriøs medicin—komplet med de store annoncer, der plejer at følge efter. Spørgsmålet nu handler ikke om psykedelika virker; det handler om, hvor hurtigt de bliver tilgængelige for dem, der har mest brug for dem.

items.title: Serotonergic psychedelics induce distinct patterns of metabolic activity and covariance within biologically informed rat brain networks.

summaries.en: Even though psilocybin, LSD, and 2C-B all work through the same brain receptor, they create surprisingly different patterns of activity in the brain — and those patterns stick around for a week after the experience ends. Scientists used brain imaging in rats to map exactly how each psychedelic reshapes the brain's metabolism, revealing drug-specific signatures that could help explain why they might work differently for different conditions. This opens a fascinating new door: rather than treating all psychedelics as interchangeable, we might be able to match specific compounds to specific mental health challenges based on their unique brain effects.
summaries.da: Selvom psilocybin, LSD og 2C-B virker gennem samme hjernereceptor, skaber de overraskende forskellige aktivitetsmønstre i hjernen — og disse mønstre bliver ved i en uge efter oplevelsen. Forskere brugte hjernescanning på rotter til at kortlægge præcis, hvordan hvert psykedelika omformer hjernens stofskifte, og afslørede stofferne hver sine særlige fingeraftryk som kunne forklare, hvorfor de virker forskelligt for forskellige tilstande. Det åbner en fascinerende ny dør: i stedet for at behandle alle psykedelika som udskiftelige, kan vi måske matche specifikke stoffer til specifikke psykiske sundhedsudfordringer baseret på deres unikke hjerneffekter.

summaries.en:
What happens when you give DMT to humans in a controlled lab setting? Scientists just found out — and it's actually pretty safe. In this study, healthy volunteers received different doses of DMT through IV infusion, and while some experienced intense effects that made them want to stop early, all side effects were mild and temporary. Here's the plot twist: smokers had roughly double the DMT levels in their blood compared to non-smokers, likely because compounds in cigarette smoke interact with how the body breaks down DMT.

Researchers ran this carefully controlled trial to nail down the basics before DMT moves into larger clinical studies — figuring out the right doses, how the drug behaves in the body, and what factors change between individuals. This kind of foundational safety work is exactly what's needed right now as psychedelics transition from underground curiosity to legitimate medicine. Every piece of solid data like this makes the path forward clearer.
summaries.da:
Hvad sker der når man giver DMT til mennesker i et kontrolleret laboratorium? Det har videnskabsmænd nu fundet ud af — og det er faktisk temmelig sikkert. I denne undersøgelse fik raske frivillige forskellige doser DMT gennem infusion i blodet, og selvom nogle fik så intense oplevelser at de ville stoppe, var alle bivirkninger milde og forbigående. Her er det spændende: rygere havde cirka det dobbelte DMT-niveau i blodet sammenlignet med ikke-rygere, sandsynligvis fordi stoffer i cigaretrøg påvirker hvordan kroppen nedbryder DMT.

Forskerne gennemførte denne nøje kontrollerede forsøg for at få styr på det grundlæggende inden DMT kommer ind i større kliniske studier — finde de rigtige doser, forstå hvordan stoffet opfører sig i kroppen, og identificere faktorer som varierer mellem individer. Netop denne slags solid sikkerhedsdata er hvad psykedelika har brug for nu, når de går fra underjordisk nysgerrighed til legitim medicin. Hver eneste opdagelse som denne gør vejen frem tydeligere.

items.title: Optimizing Ketamine Infusion Therapy for Treatment-Resistant Bipolar Depression: Commentary on Zhou et al. (2023).

summaries.en: For people with severe bipolar depression that won't respond to standard medications, ketamine infusions offer surprising hope—they can lift depression and anxiety fast, sometimes within days. A new commentary on recent research shows this approach has a solid safety track record in the short term, which is genuinely exciting news for patients who've exhausted other options. The catch? We still need to figure out who benefits most, how long the effects last, and when people need follow-up doses to prevent relapse. Researchers gave patients repeated low-dose ketamine intravenously and tracked what happened. As psychedelics and ketamine move from fringe territory into mainstream psychiatry, this work highlights what comes next: smarter ways to predict who'll respond, better tools to monitor thinking and memory during treatment, and clearer plans for keeping people well long-term. The science is pointing toward a more personalized, careful approach—not a one-size-fits-all fix, but a real option worth exploring.
summaries.da: For mennesker med svær bipolar depression, der ikke reagerer på almindelige medicin, giver ketamininfusioner overraskende håb—de kan løfte depression og angst hurtigt, nogle gange inden for dage. En ny kommentar til nylig forskning viser, at denne tilgang har et solidt sikkerhedsspor på kort sigt, hvilket er virkelig gode nyheder for patienter, der har prøvet alt andet. Hagen? Vi skal stadig finde ud af hvem der har gavn af det, hvor længe effekterne varer, og hvornår folk har brug for opfølgende doser for at forhindre tilbagefald. Forskere gav patienter gentagne lave doser ketamin intravenøst og fulgte udviklingen. Efterhånden som psykedelika og ketamin bevæger sig fra randområdet ind i psykiatrien, understreger dette arbejde hvad der kommer næste: smartere måder at forudsige hvem der reagerer, bedre værktøjer til at overvåge tænkning og hukommelse under behandling, og klarere planer for at holde folk raske længere. Videnskaben peger mod en mere personlig, omhyggelig tilgang—ikke en løsning der passer til alle, men en reel mulighed værd at udforske.

items.title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and safety of N,N -dimethyltryptamine administered intravenously in healthy smoking and non-smoking volunteers

summaries.en: Researchers just mapped out how DMT moves through the body and what it actually does — crucial groundwork before we can test it as a real treatment. The good news? It was safe in all volunteers, with only mild to moderate effects and no serious side effects. The surprise? Smokers had about twice as much DMT in their bloodstream as non-smokers, likely because something in cigarette smoke affects how the body breaks it down. Scientists gave healthy people different doses of DMT through IV infusions, measuring everything from heart rate to brain waves to subjective experience. This kind of careful pharmacological mapping is exactly what the field needs right now — it's the unglamorous but essential work that turns a promising molecule into an actual medicine. As psychedelics move from underground curiosity to legitimate clinical science, studies like this one build the foundation that lets us move safely forward.
summaries.da: Forskere har netop kortlagt, hvordan DMT bevæger sig gennem kroppen og hvad det faktisk gør — afgørende forberedelse før vi kan teste det som rigtig behandling. Det gode nyt? Det var sikkert hos alle frivillige, med kun milde til moderate effekter og ingen alvorlige bivirkninger. Overraskelsen? Rygere havde omkring dobbelt så meget DMT i blodet som ikke-rygere, sandsynligvis fordi noget i cigaretrøg påvirker, hvordan kroppen nedbryder det. Forskere gav raske personer forskellige doser DMT gennem intravenøs infusion og målte alt fra hjertehastighed til hjernebølger til subjektiv oplevelse. Denne type omhyggelig farmakologisk kortlægning er præcis hvad fagfeltet har brug for lige nu — det er det utilgloriøse men essentielle arbejde, der gør et lovende molekyle til rigtig medicin. I takt med at psykedelika bevæger sig fra underjordisk nysgerrighed til legitim klinisk videnskab, bygger studier som dette fundamentet, der lader os bevæge os sikkert fremad.

items.title: Psychedelic renaissance in healthcare: between the biomedical and the existential.

summaries.en: Right now, psychedelics are getting a lot of hype in medicine—but here's the thing: much of it is driven by companies focused on quick profits and individual wellness, which risks widening a troubling gap between pill-based treatments and the deeper, human-centered therapy that talks and stories provide. A new review digs into this tension, asking an important question: as psychedelics move into mainstream healthcare, are we missing something crucial about how they actually work—not just chemically, but in helping people make sense of their lives? The researchers argue that to get psychedelics right, we need to stop treating them as just another drug fix and start honoring the existential and narrative dimensions that make them unique in the first place.
summaries.da: Lige nu får psykedelika massiv opmærksomhed inden for medicin—men her er kernen: meget af hypen drevet af virksomheder fokuseret på hurtig profit og individuel wellness risikerer at udvide et problematisk skel mellem pille-baserede behandlinger og den dybere, menneskecentrerede terapi som samtalog fortællinger tilbyder. Et nyt review dykker ned i denne spænding og stiller et vigtig spørgsmål: mens psykedelika bevæger sig ind i mainstream sundhedsvæsenet, mister vi noget afgørende om hvordan de faktisk virker—ikke bare kemisk, men i at hjælpe mennesker med at give mening til deres liv? Forskerne argumenterer for at for at få psykedelika rigtigt må vi holde op med at behandle dem som bare endnu en drug-fix og begynde at ærer de eksistentielle og narrative dimensioner som gør dem unikke.

items.title: Hippocampal synaptic transmission and Ca<sup>2</sup>⁺ signaling are altered by the selective 5-HT<sub>2A</sub> receptor agonist, 25CN-NBOH

summaries.en: Scientists just discovered something fascinating about how psychedelics rewire a crucial brain region linked to mood and memory. When researchers exposed hippocampal neurons to a psychedelic compound, it dramatically increased communication between brain cells—boosting both the excited and calming signals neurons send each other. Here's what's wild: this happened through a completely different mechanism than previously thought, suggesting psychedelics have multiple ways of reshaping neural circuits. The team used advanced imaging and electrical recordings on mouse brain tissue to map these changes. This finding matters because while we've mapped psychedelic effects in the prefrontal cortex, the hippocampus has been largely a mystery—yet it's absolutely central to mood regulation and how we process emotions. As psychedelic research accelerates toward clinical breakthroughs, understanding these cellular mechanisms in different brain regions is key to explaining why these compounds show such remarkable promise for depression and anxiety.
summaries.da: Forskere har lige afsløret noget fascinerende om, hvordan psykedelika omstrukturerer en afgørende hjernedel, der styrer humør og hukommelse. Da forskerne eksponerede hippocampale neuroner for et psykedelika-stof, steg kommunikationen mellem hjerneceller dramatisk—med både øgede spændende og beroligende signaler mellem neuronerneHer er det vildt: det skete gennem en helt anden mekanisme end tidligere antaget, hvilket tyder på at psykedelika har flere måder at omforme neurale kredsløb på. Teamet brugte avanceret mikroskopi og elektriske målinger på musehjernenvæv til at kortlægge disse forandringer. Denne opdagelse betyder noget, fordi selv om vi har kortlagt psykedelika-effekter i præfrontal cortex, har hippocampus været stort set uudforsket—alligevel er den absolut central for humørregulering og hvordan vi behandler følelser. Mens psykedelika-forskningen accelererer mod kliniske gennembrud, er det afgørende at forstå disse cellulære mekanismer i forskellige hjernedele for at forklare, hvorfor disse stoffer viser så bemærkelsesværdig lovende resultater for depression og angst.

items.title: A randomized crossover trial comparing the acute physiological and psychological effects of botanical formulations of oral psilocybin, oral psilocin, and sublingual psilocin

summaries.en: What if you could get the therapeutic benefits of psilocybin with fewer side effects? A new study compared three different ways of taking psilocybin—the classic oral form, oral psilocin (what your body actually converts psilocybin into), and a sublingual version—all made from whole mushroom extracts. The striking finding: oral psilocin produced nearly identical psychological effects to oral psilocybin, but with notably fewer unwanted physical effects. Researchers gave 20 healthy adults these different formulations in a carefully controlled, randomized trial with therapeutic support. The results suggest that how we deliver psychedelics matters just as much as what we're delivering—and that exploring alternative routes could mean better experiences for people undergoing psychedelic-assisted therapy. This fits neatly into where the field is heading: moving beyond a one-size-fits-all approach to find personalized, optimized treatments.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis du kunne få psykedelikas terapeutiske fordele med færre bivirkninger? Et nyt studie sammenlignede tre måder at tage psilocybin på—den klassiske oral form, oral psilocin (det som din krop faktisk omdanner psilocybin til), og en sublingual version—alle lavet fra hele svampeekstrakter. Det slående fund: oral psilocin producerede næsten identiske psykologiske effekter som oral psilocybin, men med væsentligt færre uønskede fysiske effekter. Forskerne gav 20 sunde voksne disse forskellige formuleringer i et omhyggeligt kontrolleret, randomiseret forsøg med terapeutisk support. Resultaterne tyder på, at måden vi leverer psykedelika på betyder lige så meget som det, vi leverer—og at det kunne betyde bedre oplevelser for mennesker, der undergår psykedelika-assisteret terapi. Dette passer perfekt ind i hvor området bevæger sig hen: væk fra en one-size-fits-all tilgang mod at finde personaliserede, optimerede behandlinger.

items.title: Nursing education for emerging psychedelic-assisted therapy: A role-calibrated curriculum approach

summaries.en:
As psychedelic-assisted therapy moves from the lab into clinics, a crucial question emerges: who's actually trained to guide patients through these profound experiences? A new study tackles this head-on by designing a role-calibrated curriculum for nurses—the professionals who'll spend the most time with patients during psychedelic therapy sessions. The research recognizes that nursing psychedelic care isn't just about handing out pills; it's a specialized skill requiring deep knowledge of both the science and the human experience.

The study maps out what nurses at different experience levels need to know, creating a practical framework for training programs. This matters because psychedelics research is moving fast toward real-world application, and we're still figuring out how to prepare the healthcare workforce. By getting the nursing foundation right now, we're helping ensure that when psychedelic-assisted therapy becomes more widely available, patients will have skilled, knowledgeable guides ready to support them through one of the most meaningful experiences of their lives.
summaries.da:
Mens psykedelika-assisteret terapi bevæger sig fra laboratoriet ind i klinikker, dukker et afgørende spørgsmål op: hvem er egentlig uddannet til at guide patienter gennem disse dybe oplevelser? Et nyt studie griber problemet an ved at designet et rollebaseret curriculum for sygeplejersker—de fagpersoner, som tilbringer mest tid sammen med patienter under psykedelika-terapi. Forskningen erkender, at sygeplejerskefunktionen inden for psykedelika ikke bare handler om at uddele piller; det er en specialiseret færdighed, der kræver dyb viden om både videnskaben og den menneskelige erfaring.

Studiet kortlægger, hvad sygeplejersker på forskellige erfaringsniveauer har brug for at vide, og skaber dermed en praktisk ramme for træningsprogrammer. Det betyder noget, fordi psykedelika-forskningen bevæger sig hurtigt mod virkelighedens anvendelse, og vi er stadig ved at finde ud af, hvordan vi forbereder sundhedsvæsenet. Ved at få sygeplejerskegrundlaget rigtigt nu, hjælper vi med at sikre, at når psykedelika-assisteret terapi bliver mere udbredt, vil patienterne have dygtige, vidende guider klar til at støtte dem gennem en af deres mest meningsfulde oplevelser.

items.title: A randomized crossover trial comparing the acute physiological and psychological effects of botanical formulations of oral psilocybin, oral psilocin, and sublingual psilocin.

summaries.en:
Here's something practical: when researchers tested three different ways of taking psilocybin, oral psilocin (the active compound your body makes from psilocybin) worked just as well as traditional oral psilocybin—but with fewer unpleasant side effects. Sublingual psilocin also proved safe and tolerable. These aren't huge differences, but in medicine, reducing nausea and discomfort while keeping the therapeutic benefits intact matters a lot to patients actually taking these compounds.

The study involved 20 healthy adults trying different formulations in carefully controlled sessions with professional support. What this reveals is that psychedelics research is moving beyond the "one-size-fits-all" approach—scientists are now exploring whether tweaking how we administer these compounds could make therapy more accessible and comfortable. As clinical trials expand, finding formulations with better side-effect profiles could be the difference between a treatment people can actually stick with.
summaries.da:
Her er noget praktisk: da forskere testede tre forskellige måder at tage psilocybin på, virkede oral psilocin (det aktive stof dit legeme laver fra psilocybin) lige så godt som traditionel oral psilocybin—men med færre ubehagelige bivirkninger. Sublingual psilocin viste sig også sikker og veltoleret. Det er ikke massive forskelle, men inden for medicin betyder det rigtig meget for patienterne, at man kan reducere kvalme og ubehag, mens man beholder de terapeutiske fordele.

Studiet omfattede 20 raske voksne, som prøvede forskellige formuleringer i grundigt kontrollerede sessioner med professionel støtte. Det, som dette afsløres, er at psykedelika-forskning bevæger sig ud over "one-size-fits-all"-tilgangen—videnskabsmænd udforsker nu, om små ændringer i, hvordan vi administrerer disse stoffer, kunne gøre terapi mere tilgængelig og behagelig. Når kliniske forsøg udvides, kunne det at finde formuleringer med bedre bivirkningsprofiler være afgørende for, om en behandling er noget, folk kan gennemføre.

items.title: The role of BDNF promoter VI in mediating protective effects of prophylactic (R,S)-ketamine.

summaries.en: Here's something striking: a single dose of ketamine given *before* stress hits can protect your brain from depression—and now we know why. Scientists discovered that ketamine's protective power depends on a specific molecular switch in your brain called BDNF, which essentially tells your hippocampus to build new connections and bounce back stronger. Using mice genetically engineered to lack this switch, researchers showed that without it, ketamine loses its preventative punch. This opens a wild new frontier: what if we could give people at high risk of depression a small dose of ketamine before the crisis hits, like a vaccine for the mind? The study adds crucial pieces to the puzzle of how psychedelics work, suggesting that their real superpower might not just be healing existing damage but actually building resilience into our brains before we need it.
summaries.da: Her er noget bemærkelsesværdigt: en enkelt dosis ketamin givet *før* stress rammer kan beskytte din hjerne mod depression—og nu ved vi hvorfor. Forskere opdagede, at ketamins beskyttende kraft afhænger af en specifik molekylær switch i din hjerne kaldet BDNF, som grundlæggende instruerer din hippocampus til at bygge nye forbindelser og komme tilbage stærkere. Ved at bruge mus, der genetisk er modificeret til at mangle denne switch, viste forskere, at uden den mister ketamin sin forebyggende kraft. Dette åbner en vildt ny verden: hvad hvis vi kunne give mennesker i høj risiko for depression en lille dosis ketamin før krisen rammer, som en vaccine for sindet? Studiet tilføjer vigtige brikker til puslespillet om, hvordan psykedelika virker, og tyder på, at deres reelle superkraft måske ikke kun er at helbrede eksisterende skade, men faktisk at bygge modstandskraft ind i vores hjerner, før vi har brug for det.

items.title: Esketamine-based treatment, depression-specific metacognitive training, and their combination in treatment-resistant depression: 6-month trajectories of depressive symptoms and rumination in a multicenter observational study.

summaries.en: What if treating depression isn't just about feeling better—but actually changing how your mind works? New research shows that combining esketamine (a nasal spray medicine) with a specific mental training program works dramatically better than either approach alone for people with treatment-resistant depression. After six months, 92% of patients using the combination improved, compared to just 33% with either treatment solo. Crucially, the combo also reduced rumination—that exhausting mental loop where depressing thoughts trap you. Researchers tracked 46 patients in real clinical settings over half a year, measuring both mood and these deeper thought patterns that typically get stuck even when depression lifts. This fits into an exciting shift in psychedelic research: moving beyond just symptom relief toward actually rewiring the patterns underneath. The findings suggest the future of treating stubborn depression might lie in pairing psychedelics with targeted mental training—creating the conditions for real, lasting change.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis behandling af depression ikke bare handler om at få det bedre—men faktisk om at ændre, hvordan dit sind fungerer? Ny forskning viser, at kombination af esketamin (en næsespray medicin) med specifik mental træning virker dramatisk bedre end begge tilgange hver for sig for mennesker med behandlingsresistent depression. Efter seks måneder forbedrede 92% af patienter med kombinationen sig, sammenlignet med kun 33% med hver behandling alene. Vigtigst nok reducerede kombinationen også rumination—det udmattende mentale loop, hvor depressive tanker fanger dig. Forskerne fulgte 46 patienter i rigtige kliniske omgivelser over et halvt år og målte både stemning og disse dybere tankemønstre, som typisk bliver hængende selv når depression løftes. Dette passer ind i en spændende forskydning inden for psykedelika-forskningen: bevægelse væk fra bare symptomlindrings mod faktisk omstrukturering af de mønstre, der ligger under. Resultaterne tyder på, at fremtiden for behandling af stædig depression kunne ligge i at kombinere psykedelika med målrettet mental træning—skabt betingelser for reel, varig forandring.

items.title: Oregon’s state-regulated psilocybin services: Early real-world safety signals

summaries.en:
Oregon became the first place to legally offer psilocybin services to the public, and early data shows something remarkable: it's working safely. People are getting real therapeutic benefits—reduced anxiety, depression, and a genuine sense of meaning—without the serious adverse events many feared. This isn't just good news for Oregon; it's proof that psychedelics can be integrated into regulated healthcare in ways that protect people while actually helping them heal.

Researchers tracked what happens when psilocybin therapy moves from the lab into the real world, with real patients and real stakes. What they're finding fits into a much bigger picture: psychedelics are transitioning from fringe science to legitimate medicine. As more places watch Oregon's success, we're learning that the key isn't the drug itself—it's the setting, the support, and the structure around it. That changes everything about how we think treatment could work.
summaries.da:
Oregon blev det første sted, der lovligt tilbyder psykedelika-behandling til offentligheden, og tidlige data viser noget bemærkelsesværdigt: det virker sikkert. Mennesker oplever rigtig terapeutiske effekter—mindre angst, depression og en ægte følelse af mening—uden de alvorlige bivirkninger, mange frygtede. Dette er ikke bare gode nyheder for Oregon; det beviser, at psykedelika kan integreres i reguleret sundhedsvæsen på måder, der beskytter mennesker og samtidig hjælper dem til at blive raske.

Forskere fulgte, hvad der sker, når psykedelika-terapi flytter fra laboratoriet ind i den virkelige verden, med rigtige patienter og rigtige konsekvenser. Det, de finder, passer ind i et meget større billede: psykedelika går fra marginaliseret videnskab til legitim medicin. Efterhånden som flere steder følger Oregons succes, lærer vi, at nøglen ikke er stoffet selv—det er omgivelserne, støtten og strukturen omkring det. Det ændrer alt ved, hvordan vi tænker behandling kunne fungere.

items.title: Psychedelics in the treatment of anorexia nervosa: a systematic review and meta-analysis

summaries.en: What if psychedelics could help rewire the relationship people have with their bodies and food? A new systematic review is examining whether compounds like psilocybin and LSD might offer hope for those struggling with anorexia nervosa—one of the most deadly psychiatric conditions. Early signals suggest psychedelics could work differently than traditional treatments, potentially addressing the deep psychological patterns that keep eating disorders locked in place. Researchers analyzed existing studies to map what we actually know so far. This work arrives at a crucial moment: as psychedelic science moves beyond depression and PTSD, we're discovering these compounds might help with conditions that have resisted treatment for decades. It's still early, but the question itself—can psychedelics help us befriend our bodies again?—feels genuinely worth exploring.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis psykedelika kunne hjælpe mennesker til at skabe en bedre relation til deres krop og mad? En ny systematisk oversigt undersøger, om stoffer som psilocybin og LSD kunne give håb til dem, der kæmper med anoreksia nervosa—en af psykiatrien mest dødbringende sygdomme. Tidlige tegn tyder på, at psykedelika kunne virke anderledes end traditionelle behandlinger og potentielt løse de dybe psykologiske mønstre, der holder spiseforstyrrelser på plads. Forskere analyserede eksisterende studier for at kortlægge, hvad vi faktisk ved hidtil. Dette arbejde kommer på et kritisk tidspunkt: efterhånden som psykedelisk forskning bevæger sig ud over depression og PTSD, opdager vi, at disse stoffer kunne hjælpe med tilstande, som har modstået behandling i årtier. Det er stadig tidligt, men selve spørgsmålet—kan psykedelika hjælpe os til at forenes med vores kroppe igen?—føles virkelig værd at udforske.

items.title: Erratum to "Long-term treatment with esketamine nasal spray in patients with treatment resistant depression: Results from the ESCAPE-LTE study" [European Neuropsychopharmacology 107 (2026) 112801].

summaries.en:
An important correction has been issued for a major study on esketamine nasal spray, a ketamine-based treatment showing real promise for people with severe depression that hasn't responded to traditional antidepressants. The original research tracked patients over the long term, and this update ensures the findings are as accurate as possible—because when we're talking about treatments that could genuinely help people who've tried everything else, getting the details right matters.

This kind of careful science is exactly what's driving the psychedelics field forward right now. Researchers aren't just discovering that these compounds work; they're doing the meticulous work of understanding how, for whom, and what happens when people use them over months and years. Every correction, every follow-up study, every honest conversation about limitations builds the solid foundation we need to bring these treatments into wider use.
summaries.da:
En vigtig rettelse er blevet udsendt til et større studie om esketamin-næsespray, en ketamin-baseret behandling, der viser rigtig potentiale for mennesker med svær depression, som ikke reagerer på almindelige antidepressiva. Det oprindelige forskning fulgte patienter over længere tid, og denne opdatering sikrer, at findingene er så præcise som muligt—fordi når vi taler om behandlinger, der kunne hjælpe mennesker, som har prøvet alt andet, betyder detaljerne virkelig noget.

Dette slag omhyggeligt videnskab er præcis det, der driver psykedelika-forskningen fremad lige nu. Forskere handler ikke bare om at opdage, at disse stoffer virker; de udfører det omhyggelige arbejde med at forstå hvordan, for hvem, og hvad der sker, når mennesker bruger dem over måneder og år. Hver rettelse, hver opfølgningsstudie, hver ærlig samtale om begrænsninger bygger det solide fundament, vi har brug for for at få disse behandlinger i bredere brug.

items.title: Psilocybin enhances sociability only in altered behavioural state and does not need an awake experience to be effective

summaries.en:
What if a psychedelic could help people with autism without the trip? New research suggests psilocybin can boost social behaviour in mice with autism-like traits—and here's the wild part: the effect works even when the brain is anaesthetised, meaning you don't need the hallucinations or altered consciousness to get the benefit. This challenges everything we thought we knew about how psychedelics work therapeutically.

Scientists gave psilocybin to mice genetically engineered to model autism spectrum disorder and saw lasting improvements in social interaction. The breakthrough came when they tested it under anaesthesia and found the same results. This opens a fascinating door: could we eventually create autism treatments based on psychedelics that deliver the healing without the mind-altering side effects? As psychedelic research moves from counterculture curiosity into legitimate medicine, studies like this help us understand which parts of the experience actually matter for healing.
summaries.da:
Hvad hvis et psykedelikum kunne hjælpe mennesker med autisme uden at give et "trip"? Ny forskning tyder på, at psilocybin kan forbedre social adfærd hos mus med autisme-lignende træk—og her kommer det vilde: effekten virker selv når hjernen er bedøvet, hvilket betyder, at du ikke har brug for hallucinationer eller ændret bevidsthed for at få fordelen. Dette udfordrer alt, hvad vi troede, vi vidste om, hvordan psykedelika virker terapeutisk.

Forskerene gav psilocybin til mus, der var genetisk fremstillet til at modellere autismespektrumforstyrrelse, og så varige forbedringer i social interaktion. Gennembruddet kom, da de testede det under bedøvelse og fandt de samme resultater. Dette åbner en fascinerende dør: kunne vi engang udvikle autismebehandlinger baseret på psykedelika, der leverer helbredelsen uden de bevidsthedsforstyrrende bivirkninger? Når psykedelikaforskning bevæger sig fra modekulturfascination til legitim medicin, hjælper studier som dette os med at forstå, hvilke dele af oplevelsen som faktisk betyder noget for helbredelse.

items.title: Psychedelics in psychiatry: comparative effectiveness, implementation, commercialization and safety lessons learned from intranasal esketamine.

summaries.en: Esketamine—a nasal spray version of ketamine—is already helping people with severe depression in clinics across Europe and beyond. But here's what's really interesting: this real-world success story is teaching us crucial lessons about how to bring psychedelics safely and effectively into mainstream psychiatry. A new analysis looks at what esketamine's journey tells us about effectiveness, how to roll these treatments out properly, the business side of things, and most importantly, how to keep people safe. This matters because other psychedelics—like psilocybin and MDMA—are hot on its heels, and esketamine is essentially a test run showing us what works and what doesn't.
summaries.da: Esketamin—en næsespray-version af ketamin—hjælper allerede mennesker med alvorlig depression på klinikker rundt omkring i Europa og verden over. Men her er det virkelig interessante: denne succes i praksis lærer os afgørende lektioner om, hvordan man bringer psykedelika sikkert og effektivt ind i mainstream psykiatri. En ny analyse ser på, hvad esketamins rejse fortæller os om virkning, hvordan man udrullerer disse behandlinger ordentligt, forretningssiden af tingene, og vigtigst af alt, hvordan man holder mennesker sikre. Det betyder noget, fordi andre psykedelika—som psilocybin og MDMA—er lige bag efter, og esketamin er i princippet en testtur, der viser os hvad der fungerer og hvad der ikke gør.

items.title: Oncology Providers' Perspectives on Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy.

summaries.en:
Cancer doctors are getting questions about psychedelics—but most don't know how to answer. A new survey found that while nearly half of oncology providers have had patients ask about psychedelic-assisted therapy for end-of-life anxiety and depression, 80% don't feel confident counseling them. The main worry? Unknown interactions with cancer drugs and safety concerns. The good news: doctors who knew more about the emerging research were way more willing to explore it.

This study surveyed nearly 400 healthcare professionals across US cancer centers and palliative care networks. What it reveals is a critical gap—the science is moving forward, but the people actually treating patients haven't caught up yet. As psychedelic research for cancer-related suffering expands, closing this knowledge gap becomes essential. Education and access to trained treatment centers could be the missing piece that helps psychedelics reach the patients who need them most.
summaries.da:
Kræftlæger får spørgsmål om psykedelika—men de fleste ved ikke, hvordan de skal svare. En ny undersøgelse viser, at selvom næsten halvdelen af onkologiske læger har fået patienter, der spørger om psykedelika-assisteret terapi mod angst og depression ved livets slutning, føler 80% sig ikke trygge ved at vejlede dem. Hovedbekymringen? Ukendte interaktioner med kræftmedicin og sikkerhedsspørgsmål. Det gode nyhed: læger, der vidste mere om den nye forskning, var langt mere villige til at udforske det.

Denne undersøgelse omfattede næsten 400 sundhedsprofessionelle på amerikanske kræftcentre og palliativ behandling. Den afslører et kritisk tomrum—videnskaben skrider frem, men de mennesker, der faktisk behandler patienter, er ikke nået dertil endnu. Når forskningen i psykedelika mod kræftrelateret lidelse ekspanderer, bliver det afgørende at lukke dette videnshul. Uddannelse og adgang til erfarne behandlingscentre kunne være det manglende stykke, der hjælper psykedelika til de patienter, der har mest brug for det.

items.title: Development of Japanese Versions of the 4-Item Mystical Experience Questionnaire and 7-Item Challenging Experience Questionnaire.

summaries.en: When people take psychedelics in clinical settings, researchers need to measure what they actually experience — the profound, mystical moments and the challenging, difficult ones. Scientists have now created shorter Japanese versions of the key questionnaires used to capture these experiences, cutting down from 30 and 26 questions to just 4 and 7. This matters because it means faster assessments and less burden on participants, while keeping what makes these tools valuable. The study involved careful translation work guided by international standards, ensuring the questions feel natural and make sense for Japanese speakers. As psychedelic therapy edges closer to real-world use globally, having reliable measurement tools in different languages becomes essential — this is about making sure research can happen anywhere, and that the incredible experiences people have aren't lost in translation.
summaries.da: Når mennesker tager psykedelika i kliniske forsøg, skal forskere måle hvad de oplever — de dybe, mystiske øjeblikke og de udfordrende, vanskelige. Videnskabsfolk har nu skabt kortere japanske versioner af de vigtigste spørgeskemaer, der bruges til at indfange disse oplevelser, reduceret fra 30 og 26 spørgsmål til blot 4 og 7. Det betyder hurtigere vurderinger og mindre belastning på deltagerne, samtidig med at værktøjernes styrke bevares. Arbejdet involverede omhyggelig oversættelse ifølge internationale standarder, som sikrer at spørgsmålene føles naturlige for japansk-talende. Når psykedelisk terapi nærmer sig faktisk verdensomspændende brug, bliver pålidelige måleredskaber på forskellige sprog afgørende — det handler om at forskning kan ske overalt, og at de utrolige oplevelser mennesker har ikke går tabt i oversættelsen.

items.title: AMCP Market Insights: Optimizing managed care approaches to treatment-resistant depression.

summaries.en:
When standard antidepressants don't work—and for some people they simply don't—life can feel stuck. Treatment-resistant depression affects millions, draining quality of life and straining healthcare systems. Now psilocybin is emerging as a genuinely promising option for people who've tried everything else. A panel of healthcare leaders recently gathered to figure out how to actually make this work in practice: who should get it, how do we know it's worth the cost, and crucially, do we have enough trained therapists to guide people through the experience safely?

The study mapped out where psychedelic-assisted therapy fits into depression care right now—and it's clear the field is moving fast. Experts agree the evidence is real but want more data comparing psilocybin to other options and understanding exactly which patients benefit most. The biggest practical challenge? Building a real network of mental health professionals trained to administer and support these treatments. As psychedelics shift from research labs into actual healthcare systems, these questions matter enormously for patients waiting for hope.
summaries.da:
